newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hundreds march in HK over Chinese dissidents.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds march in HK over Chinese dissidents.

text.p: Hundreds of demonstrators took to the streets in Hong Kong on Sunday to press Beijing for the release of Chinese dissidents.

"Suppression is shameful...Speech is innocent," chanted the protesters as they marched from the central business district to the headquarters of Xinhua news agency, China's de facto embassy in the British colony.

Brandishing banners and placards, they called for the release of detained Chinese dissidents including Wang Dan and Liu Xiaobo, saying their imprisonment was a violation of their freedom of speech and thought.
This month, China charged Wang, a leading figure in the 1989 Beijing pro-democracy movement, with plotting to overthrow the government.
Beijing has also sentenced prominent literary critic Liu to three years in a labour camp.

In the past week, Beijing condemned as illegal the escape of dissident Wang Xizhe from China to the United States via Hong Kong. Pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong fear China will shut down the escape route after the handover.
China also declared that Hong Kong people should not organise political activities that attack internal affairs in the mainland after the sovereignty transfer.

Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen hinted to the Asian Wall Street Journal that Hong Kong activists would not be able to mark the bloody June 4, 1989, crackdown on pro-democracy protests in Tiananmen Square.
Legislator Emily Lau, who participated in Sunday's March, said Qian's remarks could hit confidence in Hong Kong.
"He seemed to be warning Hong Kong's media they could not criticize Beijing. I think it's regretable," she said. "Hong Kong people are very concerned about human rights in China."
The Sunday march was organised by the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriot Democratic Movements in China, which Beijing has branded as subversive.
